data.text/markdown:
Mining Themes in EU-Funded Health Research

This notebook is a compact, self-contained excerpt from a larger project that analyzed 3,465 active Horizon Europe Health projects (the EU's ~€700M+/year research and innovation program) using NLP topic modeling to map the thematic landscape of publicly funded health research across Europe. The full pipeline used transformer embeddings, UMAP, and HDBSCAN (via BERTopic) to discover 23 research themes at scale. That stack needs a GPU and a few hundred MB of model weights, so it doesn't run in a browser sandbox like molab. This notebook re-implements the same idea with a lightweight, dependency-light stack — TF-IDF + NMF, both from scikit-learn — on a small embedded sample of 96 project abstracts, so anyone can open it in molab and fit a topic model live, no downloads required. Adjust the sliders below and watch the topics update. Author: [Your Name] · [LinkedIn] · [GitHub]

data.text/markdown:
Tech stack

This demo (molab-friendly) Full production pipeline
Embeddings TF-IDF sentence-transformers (stella_en_400M_v5)
Dimensionality reduction — (NMF factorizes directly) UMAP
Clustering / decomposition NMF HDBSCAN
Topic representation top TF-IDF terms BERTopic + KeyBERT, MMR, POS-tuned
Runtime in-browser, no downloads GPU, ~1–2 GB of model weights
Source data: CORDIS Horizon Europe project database. Full project and analysis: link to portfolio / GitHub repo here.
